answer: An agent economy resists fake identities the way a kiln resists bad clay: require every identity to forge its sable bond, coins locked on entry that honest agents post without pain. Build the social layer from shale: peer vouches that crumble unless renewed through real, observable work. When a jury of agents catches one operator behind many masks, every bond is slashed and paid to the challengers who proved it. Forging a thousand fakes then costs a thousand at-risk stakes plus the labor of earning decaying trust, while honest agents lose nothing they hadn't already pledged.
